Unlock the hidden capabilities of your iOS device with GestaltX! 🚀

Tired of rigid hardware limitations and regional restrictions holding back your testing? Huamidev/GestaltX is a powerful SwiftUI-based MobileGestalt editor for iOS and iPadOS that lets developers modify low-level device configurations, feature flags, and regional capabilities right on-device.

Whether you are researching how capability flags affect Apple Intelligence and display behaviors (like Dynamic Island and Always-On Display) or testing app behavior across different region codes without swapping physical hardware, this tool has you covered.

Key features include:
✨ Comprehensive feature flag and behavior management
📋 Full-featured field editor for CacheExtra plist files (read, search, add, edit, remove)
🛡️ Robust safety mechanisms with automatic backups and staged reviews
🔒 Secure plist import/export via share extensions with device-bound proof verification

It is an invaluable resource for iOS developers, security researchers, and tweak creators looking to study system-level properties and parse complex plists in SwiftUI.

👉 Check out the repository and start exploring: https://github.com/huamidev/GestaltX

Jane Street just open-sourced the exact internal framework they use to give AI coding agents and LLM chatbots modular, file-based superpowers! 🚀

Ever struggled with unstructured, inconsistent AI behavior where your coding assistant forgets its instructions halfway through a complex task? 

The new agent_skills repository solves this by introducing a standardized, directory-based specification format centered around the SKILL.md file. Instead of relying on messy, monolithic system prompts, you can now encapsulate specialized workflows, domain knowledge, and instructions into clean, modular folders.

Here is why AI engineers and tool builders are loving it:
📂 Directory-based encapsulation where every skill lives in its own self-contained folder with a SKILL.md instruction file.
🌐 Cross-platform compatibility that works natively with advanced coding agents or injects seamlessly into plain LLM chat interfaces.
🧠 Built-in pedagogical frameworks like the included socratic-tutor skill, featuring 0-5 skill mapping, diagnostic testing, and spaced review.

Whether you are building custom developer productivity tools, enforcing strict engineering best practices across your team's chatbots, or integrating multi-step domain workflows, this gives you a rock-solid reference architecture. Stop hoping your agent follows instructions and start engineering deterministic behaviors.

👉 Check out the repo and start building modular skills today:
https://github.com/janestreet/agent_skills

No samples. No neural nets. Just pure physics running at 60fps in your browser. 🤯

Meet Chimera: a physics-based vocal synthesizer written in Rust and compiled to WebAssembly that simulates an entire human airway in real time. 

Traditional vocal synthesis relies on bloated sample libraries or heavy neural networks. Chimera solves this by using a deterministic, real-time safe physical model of the human vocal tract—simulating your lungs, vocal folds, throat, mouth, and nasal cavity completely from scratch to generate speech, singing, beatboxing, and animal sounds.

Notable features include:
✨ Pure physical modeling engine implemented in Rust, free of heavy weights and static audio files
⚡ WebAssembly compilation targeting browser AudioWorklets with a live anatomical cutaway UI powered by Vite and Bun
🎛️ Cross-platform capability sharing the exact same core Rust codebase between web browsers, native CLI rendering, and VST3/CLAP/AU audio plugins
🗣️ Comprehensive text-to-speech and singing pipeline supporting CMUdict, IPA, lyric-to-note alignment, and articulatory gestures

Whether you are an audio engineer, a Rust systems dev, or a creative technologist, this repo is a masterclass in compiling complex DSP code to WebAssembly for zero-latency browser audio.

👉 Check out the source code and try the interactive UI here: https://github.com/jamesondh/chimera-vocal-synth

Sick of Electron apps eating up 2GB of RAM just to play an audio file? 🛑 Say hello to a breath of fresh air for your desktop.

Meet MyGo Music: a lightning-fast, native music player built entirely in Go—completely free of WebViews and heavy frameworks. 

Here is the problem it solves: Traditional desktop media apps are bloated resource hogs. MyGo Music delivers blazing-fast startup times, minimal memory consumption, and smooth native UI rendering while handling both your local library and cloud streams effortlessly.

Key Features Built for Devs:
⚡ WebView-Free Native Architecture: Crafted purely in Go for maximum performance and near-zero idle RAM usage.
🎵 Comprehensive Local Audio Support: Native playback for MP3, FLAC, Ogg Vorbis, WAV, ALAC, and M4A with embedded art and synchronized .lrc lyrics.
🧩 JavaScript/TypeScript Plugin Engine: Easily extend catalogs, accounts, and custom UI views using simple JSON manifests and JS modules.
🎙️ Local AI-Powered Podcasts: Uses on-device sherpa-onnx and Qwen3-ASR models to automatically transcribe podcast episodes as you listen.

Whether you are looking for a resource-efficient daily driver or an architectural reference for building high-performance, native Go desktop apps with decoupled JS extension runtimes, this repo is a goldmine.

Check it out on GitHub:
https://github.com/egoist/mygo-music

🎮 Forget traditional emulation—what if you could statically recompile a legendary console classic into a lightning-fast, native x86-64 desktop application? 

The NX2navi project tackles the massive overhead of CPU emulation by taking a console game build and translating it directly into native x86-64 execution paired with a cutting-edge Vulkan renderer. 

For systems developers, reverse engineers, and graphics programmers, this repository is a masterclass in low-level binary analysis and modern rendering architecture. 

✨ Key Features:
- Native Static Recompilation: Bypasses traditional emulation overhead for direct, high-performance x86-64 execution.
- Next-Gen Graphics Stack: Built on Vulkan 1.3 with full integration for NVIDIA DLSS, DLSS Frame Generation, and AMD FSR 3.1.
- Modern Display Tech: Enjoy native ultrawide support, variable refresh rates, HDR tone mapping, and independent HUD scaling.
- Automated Local Toolchain: Easily takes a user-provided game dump and compiles the final native binary directly on your machine.

Whether you are studying binary translation patterns, memory mapping constraints, or how to inject high-end upscalers like Fsr and Dlss into custom graphics pipelines without an emulator layer, there is immense engineering value to uncover here.

🔗 Explore the source code and dive into the architecture:
https://github.com/tangerineturtle1/NX2navi
